issue.title: Stand up a link-shortener service (POST /shorten, GET /{code} redirect)
issue.description: Greenfield: build a small HTTP service that shortens URLs. POST /shorten returns a 7-char code; GET /{code} 302-redirects; unknown or expired codes 404; codes survive an api restart (persistence).

fixture.explore_findings: The repo is a fresh scaffold: a BRIEF.md, a RUNBOOK.md, and a config file — no source directories, no services, no compose file, no datastore, no CI. There is no established architecture to inherit; the runnable surface is empty. No sibling spec in the project carries an architecture proposal.

question: Should prep's conditional architecture step fire on this issue — fire or skip?
_comment: The canonical fire case: a new runnable system (HTTP service + datastore for persistence-across-restart) with an empty runnable surface and no architecture to inherit, and no existing sibling proposal. Every clause of the new-runnable-surface trigger is satisfied, so the precision-biased rule fires unambiguously.
